instructions: At least 2 hours ahead, or the day before: rinse the 1 cup rice in a sieve until the water runs clear. Put it in a medium pot with 3 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt and bring it to a boil over high heat.

Stir it, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, until the rice is very soft and the water is gone. Mash it lightly with a potato masher, spread it out in a wide bowl and leave it until it's completely cool, then cover and refrigerate it. Warm rice makes the yogurt split. If you have about 4 cups of soft leftover rice, use that instead.

Whisk the 2 1/2 cups yogurt and 1/2 cup milk together until smooth. Add them to the cold rice with the last 1/4 tsp salt and mix until there are no dry clumps. It should be thick but loose enough to spoon, so stir in a few spoonfuls of water if it's stiff.
Peel and finely grate the carrot. Grate the cucumber and squeeze out the water with your hands. Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro. Stir all three into the rice.
Peel and mince 1 tsp of the ginger. Roughly chop the 1/4 cup cashews.

For the tadka, heat the 1 tbsp oil in a small frying pan over medium. Add the 1 tsp mustard seeds and 1 tsp cumin seeds. When the mustard seeds start to pop, add the 1 1/2 tsp chana dal, 1 1/2 tsp urad dal, the cashews and the 2 dried chilies, broken in half.

Stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the dals and cashews are golden. Add the ginger and 2 sprigs of curry leaves and stir for about 30 seconds, until the leaves are crisp. Stand back a little. They spatter. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the pinch of asafoetida.
Pour the tadka, oil and all, over the curd rice and stir it through. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Serve cool or at room temperature.
advance_prep_notes: cook the rice at least 2 hours ahead so it's cold, or the day before
method_notes: All three cook the rice softer than usual, mash it lightly and cool it completely before the yogurt goes in, then pour over a tempering of mustard seeds, urad dal, dried red chili, curry leaves, ginger and hing. Swasthi's uses about 1 1/4 cups yogurt for every 1/2 cup raw rice, adds chana dal, grated carrot and cucumber and optional cashews, and makes milk optional. Hebbar's temple style loosens the yogurt with milk and a little cream and adds cashews, raisins and pomegranate; Cook with Manali mixes in 1/2 cup milk and chills it for a few hours before serving. This one follows Swasthi's ratios for four, with a little milk to keep it soft and the cashews in for crunch.
